accountDeletionDesc: Permanently delete your account, with the workspaces only you own.
accountDeletionWarning: This can’t be reversed. Your account is deleted, and you leave every workspace you share with others. The workspaces below that you own are deleted too, and everyone else in them loses access:
accountDeletionWarningNoWorkspaces: This can’t be reversed. Your account is deleted, and you leave every workspace you share with others.
accountDeletionConfirmLabel: Confirm by typing this account’s email.
accountDeletionBlockedLastAdministrator: You’re this server’s only administrator. Make someone else an administrator before you delete your account.
accountDeletionBlockedSharedOrganization: Your organization holds workspaces other people own. Ask a server administrator to delete your account; they choose who takes over ownership.
accountDeletionMismatch: The email doesn’t match your account
accountDeletionBusy: Another operation is in progress in one of your workspaces. Try again shortly.

accountDeletionLegalHoldPerson: A legal hold keeps your account. Ask your organization to release it first.

serverAccountsAddBody: Move between other Leafen servers or accounts on this device.

move.title: Move to another server
move.meta: Move this workspace to another Leafen server that people already use, or move one here.
move.outHelp: On the receiving server, create a new workspace and start it with “Move from another server” to get a code, then paste it here. That server needs this version or newer.
move.pairsHelp: Match each person here with an account on {{address}}. Their writing and comments then carry over to that account. Anyone not matched stays as a name, and can be matched later in Settings → People → Imported people.
move.stays: From the start of the move no one can change this workspace here. Pages only someone else can read stay here.
move.failed: The move stopped, and the workspace accepts changes again as before. To try again, paste the same code again. If it isn’t taken, create a new one on the other server.
move.moved: This workspace moved to {{address}}. It no longer accepts changes here.
move.pagesLeft: Pages only other people can read weren’t moved and stay here.
move.notCarried: People matched with an account there keep their membership and page shares. Others are listed there to invite, and public links and sites arrive turned off, to turn on again at the new address.
move.movedPeopleTitle: {{count}} people weren’t matched with an account here
move.movedPeopleHelp: They worked in this workspace on the old server. Invite them to work together again, then share again the pages that were shared with them.
move.movedPublicTitle: {{count}} pages were public on the old server
move.movedPublicHelp: They came here private. Open each and turn its web link or site on again from Share.
move.movedHelp: It stays here as read-only. Delete it from the danger zone when you no longer need it.
move.inNeedsEmpty: Only a workspace with no pages can receive one. In the workspace menu, choose New workspace and start it with “Move from another server”.
move.inHelp: Creates a code valid for an hour that fills this empty workspace with a workspace from another Leafen server.
move.inCodeHelp: Paste it in the workspace’s settings on the other server, under Move this workspace, before {{time}}. It lets only that server connect to this workspace: don’t share it.
move.inFailed: Importing the workspace failed. Create a new code to try again.
move.alreadyHere: This server already has this workspace’s pages: it was moved or imported here before. Nothing was imported.
move.alreadyThere: The other server already has this workspace’s pages: it was moved or imported there before. The workspace accepts changes again as before.
move.movedIn: A workspace moved here: {{pages}} pages, {{files}} files, {{comments}} comments.
move.codeInvalid: The other server doesn’t take this code. It may have expired, or the other server restarted and no longer has it. Create a new one on the other server.
move.sameServer: This code was made on this server. The workspace is already here, so it can’t move here; a workspace moves only to another Leafen server. To have its pages in another workspace on this server, copy them there with Move to in the page’s ⋯ menu.
move.notEmpty: Only an empty workspace can receive a moved workspace; create a new one first.
move.requestFailed: The other server didn’t accept the move. Check that its address is reachable from here and try again.
move.moreAccounts: More accounts — search by name or email

webhookSecretDescription: Check each delivery’s signature with it. It’s shown only now.
webhookRemoveConfirmDetail: Leafen stops sending events to this address. To get them again, add the address again; it gets a new secret.
webhookAddressNotPublic: Leafen sends to addresses on the internet. This one is on this computer or a private network, which Leafen can’t send to.
webhookAddressInvalid: Enter a web address that starts with https:// (or http://).

Browsers, apps and agents such as Claude Code connect at the address as it is. To use a connector, use Leafen’s Tailscale (free public address), your own Cloudflare tunnel, or an address opened on port 443.

page.content_updated: What’s on a page changes, like a block added or removed. Several of these in quick succession arrive as one event.

page.deleted: A page goes to Trash. If page.undeleted follows shortly after, the two cancel out.
page.locked: Someone locks a page so it can’t be edited.

page.undeleted: A page comes back from Trash. If page.deleted follows shortly after, the two cancel out.

database.content_updated: Something inside a database changes, like a child page added or removed. Several of these in quick succession arrive as one event.
database.created: A database is made. Changes made to it right after arrive as their own events.
database.deleted: A database goes to Trash. If database.undeleted follows shortly after, the two cancel out.
database.moved: A database moves somewhere else. Several of these in quick succession arrive as one event.
database.schema_updated: A database’s schema changes: a property is added, removed or given another type. Several of these in quick succession arrive as one event.
database.undeleted: A database comes back from Trash. If database.deleted follows shortly after, the two cancel out.

data_source.content_updated: Something inside a data source changes, like a child page added or removed. Several of these in quick succession arrive as one event.
data_source.schema_updated: A data source’s schema changes: a property is added, removed or given another type. Several of these in quick succession arrive as one event.
data_source.created: A data source is made. Changes made to it right after arrive as their own events.
data_source.moved: A data source moves somewhere else. Several of these in quick succession arrive as one event.
data_source.deleted: A data source goes to Trash. If data_source.undeleted follows shortly after, the two cancel out.
data_source.undeleted: A data source comes back from Trash. If data_source.deleted follows shortly after, the two cancel out.

view.created: A database gets a new view. Changes made to it right after arrive as their own events.
view.updated: A view’s filters, sorts, shown properties or other settings change. Several of these in quick succession arrive as one event.
view.deleted: A database loses one of its views.

comment.created: Someone adds a comment to a discussion or as a suggestion.

file_upload.created: Someone starts a new file upload.
file_upload.expired: A file upload ran out of time before the file was sent and attached.
file_upload.upload_failed: Importing a file from an external URL into a Leafen upload failed.

webhooks.verifyNeeded: Verify the endpoint to receive webhook events.
webhooks.verifyNeededNote: Events start once the verification token sent to the webhook URL comes back, so they reach only whoever holds that address.
webhooks.deleteDetail: The webhook URL gets no more events. To receive them again, create a new subscription.
webhooks.verifyDescription:
A verification token was sent to the webhook URL.
Enter it below to turn the subscription on.
webhooks.tokenMismatch: That isn’t the right verification token.
webhooks.failedEventsDescription: See which events didn’t reach the webhook URL, to track down what went wrong.

mcpToken.missing: This MCP token can’t be found

mcpToken.notKept: This token can’t be shown again. Refresh it to make a new one you can see any time.
mcpToken.previousUntil: The previous token keeps working until {{date}}
mcpToken.refreshDetail: A new MCP token is made at once. Put it in place of the old one in your MCP clients or agents so they keep working.
mcpToken.refreshWhen: When should the current MCP token be revoked?
mcpToken.revokeLaterNote: Until {{date}} the current MCP token still works. Give your MCP clients or agents the new one before then so nothing stops.
mcpToken.revokeNowNote: Refreshing stops the current MCP token at once. MCP clients or agents still using it are cut off until they get the new token.
mcpToken.toolsDescription: The tools this MCP client is allowed to call.

mcpToken.handsAllOverDescription: Turned on, an agent with this token deletes from Trash for good, changes sharing, publishing or permissions, changes members or guests, and manages accounts, backups or the organization without asking you. Turned off, as a token starts, it asks you first in your conversation with it. The agent asks you in the conversation and passes your answer on, and Leafen can’t tell your answer from one the agent makes up. Everyday work, such as moving to the trash, writing and moving, never asks. The agent can turn this on in your conversation too, asking you once; turning it off doesn’t ask. An administrator’s safeguards, such as approving every app action, still ask while it’s on.
mcpToken.notionOnlyToolsDescription: Turned on, this token’s tool list names every tool of Notion’s MCP: the Notion-style tools (notion-*) Leafen has, and those it doesn’t have, such as folders, skills, agents, sessions, calendar, meeting notes and AI search, which only answer that Leafen doesn’t have them and what to use instead. Turned off, as a token starts, the list holds Leafen’s core tools, and an agent finds the rest or turns the Notion-style tools on in the conversation. Any tool called by its name still answers. Turn it on for an agent written against Notion’s own list of tools.
mcpToken.dangerDescription: Deleting this MCP client revokes its token for good and disconnects it from this workspace.
mcpToken.removeDetail: The MCP token is revoked for good and this MCP client leaves the workspace. A client or agent still using the token is cut off.
mcpToken.accessDescription: These are the pages and databases this MCP client can reach.
mcpToken.noPagesNote: It reaches no page. Choose pages with “Edit access” or turn on All pages.
mcpToken.pagesNote: It reaches only these pages and the pages under them. Tools that can’t be held to pages (moving, duplicating, databases, views, files, the API and others) don’t work.
mcpToken.managersOwnerNote: Only the person who created this token can manage its page access
mcpToken.allPagesNote: It reaches every page you can see, including ones made later. Turn it off to narrow it to the pages you choose and the pages under them.

removeOwnsWorkspace: Pass on the workspace they own first.
